descriptors.concept_name: Disclosures in Offer Documents and Lead Manager Obligations
descriptors.definition: Offer documents must provide true and adequate material disclosures to help applicants make informed investment decisions. Lead managers are obligated to exercise due diligence regarding issue aspects and ensure that financial statements are not more than six months old.
instrument_references: Schedule VI of SEBI ICDR Regulations
inclusion: Material disclosures in draft and final offer documents
Financial statements dating within six months of issue opening
Certificates and due diligence by lead managers
nearby_distinctions: Differs from general ongoing periodic disclosures under LODR regulations by focusing specifically on initial capital issuance documents.

descriptors.concept_name: Disclosures in the Draft Offer Document and the Offer Document
descriptors.definition: Offer documents must contain true and adequate material disclosures under the Companies Act and relevant schedules to guide investor decisions. Lead managers must verify issue aspects and confirm that financial statement particulars are current within six months.
inclusion: Disclosures required by the Companies Act and SEBI schedules
Due diligence by lead managers on all issue aspects
nearby_distinctions: Focuses on mandatory disclosures within the offer document lifecycle rather than general stock exchange disclosures.

descriptors.concept_name: Filing of the Draft Offer Document and Offer Documents (Regulation 123)
descriptors.definition: Issuers must file multiple copies of draft offer documents along with specified fees and due diligence certificates with the Board prior to a further public offer. The Board reviews these documents and may issue observations or mandate changes within a specified timeframe.
inclusion: Submission of draft offer documents to the Board and stock exchanges
Filing of required certificates from lead managers and debenture trustees
Incorporation of Board observations into an updated draft document
nearby_distinctions: Focuses on regulatory pre-issue filing and observation clearance rather than the final public circulation stage.

descriptors.concept_name: Draft Offer Document and Offer Document to be Available to the Public (Regulation 124)
descriptors.definition: Draft offer documents must be hosted on designated websites for public comments for at least twenty-one days accompanied by a public announcement in newspapers. Issuers and lead managers must ensure that publicly hosted versions match those filed with regulatory authorities.
inclusion: Public availability of draft offer documents for comments
Newspaper announcements of document filing
Filing of public comment details and consequential modifications
nearby_distinctions: Focuses on public feedback collection and transparency obligations rather than the initial internal regulatory filing.

descriptors.definition: Issuers determine share prices, conversion prices, or coupon rates in consultation with lead managers or through the book building mechanism. Final prospectuses filed with the Registrar of Companies must reflect a single price or specific coupon rate.
inclusion: Face value disclosure alongside price band or issue price
Pricing determination via book building or consultation
Price band constraints and floor price announcements
exclusion: Post-listing secondary market price stabilization mechanisms
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between fixed price issues and book-built issue pricing frameworks.

descriptors.definition: The face value of equity shares must be clearly disclosed alongside the price band or issue price in all draft offer documents, offer documents, advertisements, and application forms. This disclosure must use an identical font size to ensure prominence and clarity for investors.
inclusion: Face value disclosure in offer documents and advertisements
Uniform font size requirement across application materials
nearby_distinctions: Centers purely on face value disclosure formatting rather than pricing determination formulas.

descriptors.definition: An issuer establishes equity share prices, conversion prices, and coupon rates either through consultations with lead managers or by executing a formal book building process. The book building procedure must strictly follow the operational rules specified in the applicable schedule.
inclusion: Price determination consultation with lead managers
Book building execution methodology
exclusion: Fixed-price allocation procedures handled outside book building
nearby_distinctions: Emphasizes the mechanism of price discovery over statutory disclosures of face value or price bands.

descriptors.definition: Issuers specify fixed prices or price bands in offer documents and determine final prices prior to filing prospectuses with the Registrar of Companies. The cap on a price band must remain within specified percentage thresholds above the floor price, which cannot fall below the security face value.
inclusion: Floor price and price band limits relative to face value
Percentage constraints between price band caps and floors
Pre-bid advertisements and financial ratio disclosures
nearby_distinctions: Focuses on numerical boundary constraints for price bands rather than general pricing consultation procedures.

descriptors.definition: Issuers may offer specified securities at varied prices to specific categories such as retail investors, employees, or anchor investors under prescribed discount thresholds. Any price discount or cross-issue pricing difference must be explicitly justified and expressed in rupee terms within the offer document.
inclusion: Discount limits for retail investors and employees
Pricing parity rules for anchor investors
Justification requirements for composite issue price variations
exclusion: Discriminatory pricing outside permitted regulatory categories
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes uniform pricing rules from permitted exceptions allowing targeted discounts for specific investor classes.

descriptors.definition: This framework governs the procedural requirements and category-wise allocation quotas for public issues conducted through book building. It establishes mandatory distribution percentages across retail, non-institutional, and qualified institutional buyer categories.
inclusion: Procedural conditions for public issues
Allocation frameworks across investor categories
nearby_distinctions: Focuses on post-pricing allocation mechanics rather than the initial pricing determination stages.

descriptors.definition: Net offer allocations in book-built issues must adhere to prescribed minimum and maximum percentage quotas designated for retail individual investors, non-institutional investors, and qualified institutional buyers. Subscriptions within these categories permit specific spillover adjustments and sub-allocations for mutual funds and anchor investors.
inclusion: Category-wise quota percentages for book-built issues
Mutual fund and anchor investor sub-allocations
Non-institutional investor application size sub-reservations
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between institutional and retail quotas while enforcing strict internal caps within non-institutional brackets.

descriptors.definition: Issuers may carve out competitive reservations from the issue size excluding promoter contributions for eligible employees and specific shareholders. These reservations are subject to strict percentage limits, individual allotment caps, and rules governing unsubscribed portion adjustments.
inclusion: Reservations for employees and eligible shareholders
Caps on employee and shareholder reservation percentages
Rules for handling under-subscription and spillover into net public offers
exclusion: Reservations for lead managers, registrars, or syndicate members
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes targeted competitive reservations from standard net public offer allocations.
